sentences.text: Vipin .....Applicant(s) Versus State of U.P. .....Opposite Party(s) Counsel for Applicant(s) :
Bharat Singh Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
G.A. Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J. 1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Bharat Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 567 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Dataganj, District Budaun, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by about 11 days from the date of death of the deceased person and is delayed by about 15 days from the date of occurrence and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased person.

5. Learned counsel has next stated that the deceased was taken for treatment by the applicant only and there was no whispering of any complaint against the applicant or any other person by the prosecution.
Even the informant was present at the time of inquest proceedings undertaken on 01.12.2023 but he did not care to institute the FIR, as such it is a clear cut case of false implication.
The cause of death has been found to be septicemia due to ante mortem burn injury.
There is no dying declaration of the deceased person, as such the applicant is entitled for bail.
6. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.12.2023 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record and taking into consideration the delay in institution of the FIR and the informant being present at the time of inquest proceedings, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Vipin, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Krishan Pahal,J.) September 8, 2025 Sumit S  Vipin vs State Of U.P. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38314190/
